purpose: Pramipexole is used to treat the symptoms of Parkinson's disease, such as tremors, stiffness, and difficulty moving. It is also used to treat Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS), a condition that causes uncomfortable sensations in your legs and an urge to move them, especially at night. This medication can help you move more easily and sleep better.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical called dopamine to help control movement and coordination. In Parkinson's disease and RLS, your brain does not make enough dopamine. Pramipexole works by acting like dopamine in your brain, essentially 'pretending' to be dopamine so your brain gets the signal it needs. This helps reduce your symptoms and makes it easier to move and feel comfortable.
common_side_effects: Nausea or upset stomach, dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up), drowsiness or feeling very sleepy, headache, constipation, dry mouth, and swelling in your legs or feet. Some people may have unusual dreams or trouble sleeping.
warnings: This medication can make you very drowsy or even cause you to suddenly fall asleep without warning, so be very careful when driving or using machines. Some people develop strong urges they cannot control, such as gambling, eating, shopping, or sexual urges — tell your doctor right away if this happens. Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause serious problems. Let your doctor know if you have kidney problems, since your dose may need to be adjusted.
typical_dosing: For Parkinson's disease, you usually start with a low dose taken three times a day, and your doctor will slowly increase it over several weeks to find the right amount for you. For Restless Legs Syndrome, it is usually taken once a day about 2 to 3 hours before bedtime. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly, and never change your dose on your own.
